novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanism-focused hypothesis—whether TSFMs represent “the reproduction-number threshold mechanism, not just curve momentum”—using the specific “matched-curve/opposite-R counterfactual,” rather than merely applying a standard probe to epidemic data. Searches for “time-series foundation model mechanistic interpretability reproduction number threshold,” “TSFM epidemic R_t probing,” and “matched-curve counterfactual turning-point representation” found no essentially equivalent study; the closest methodological prior is “What Do World Models Learn in RL? Probing Latent Representations in Learned Environment Simulators” (2026), which uses probing and causal steering but studies game-state variables, while “Decoding Latent Spaces: Assessing the Interpretability of Time Series Foundation Models” (2025) examines general TSFM latent structure without mechanistic thresholds. The step from these works is not a direct transfer because the claim introduces the new core relationship between an epidemiological threshold and momentum-matched internal representations, although its probes and steering are standard and the epidemic setting makes it a focused, within-framework advance rather than a new general interpretability paradigm; this supports a high-novelty score of 7 rather than 8–10.
